messages:
maria: quick question re: rollout metadata — should we encode a separate "soft-expiry hint" that clients can use to start probing replacements before the authoritative pin TTL expires?
kevin: I've been thinking about this too. soft-expiry would be advisory only (no forced eviction). TTL stays authoritative. makes sense for early warmups/failovers.
anita: +1 but watch size. metadata is replicated a lot. prefer tiny, flat fields (numbers/short enums) not nested blobs. e.g. expiry_hint_secs and eviction_priority (0-255).
ryan: compatibility note: old clients will ignore new keys, which is fine. routers however read these fields to decide fallback order — so router rollouts need to tolerate missing keys and have sane defaults.
sasha: quick proposal, very compact schema example:
```
{
  "pin_ttl": 86400,            // authoritative TTL in secs
  "expiry_hint": 300,         // advisory: start probing/replacement X secs before TTL
  "fallback_order": ["v2-quant","v1"],
  "hint_version": "1"
}
```
maria: do we actually need hint_version? i think yes so semantics can evolve.
kevin: also thinking about a probe contract so clients know how aggressive to probe: min interval, max tries. nested object is convenient but we should flatten to keep size down. e.g. probe_min_s, probe_max_tries.
anita: flattened + checksum for variant identity. add model_fp (sha256 hex) to avoid racey swaps. keep everything < 1KB.
ryan: ops side: routers and stores must treat unknown fields as opt-in and default to old behaviour. Migration plan idea:
- v1: current pins (pin_ttl only)
- v2: adds expiry_hint, probe_* fields, fallback_order
Default: missing fields => no hint, fallback = model/catalog order.
sasha: tenant override edge-case: if a tenant sets pin override we overwrite pin_ttl but we should NOT implicitly overwrite expiry_hint unless they explicitly set it. document explicitly.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: rollout-meta-schema-v2 -> staging @ 2024-11-04T11:00:00Z
maria: UX: expose expiry_hint on model page and show probe settings under advanced so SREs can tune.
kevin: one last practical ask: can we keep metadata flat-keyed (no nested maps) and keep total serialized size < 1KB? yes, with the above fields.
anita: I'll draft the RFC follow-up with concrete examples, the compatibility matrix, and a migration plan. assigning @kevin for router changes and @ryan for datastore migration.
maria: thank you — i'll expect the RFC PR. closing unless anything else. :+1:
